newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul summons Japanese envoy over boat seizure.
newsitem.headline: Seoul summons Japanese envoy over boat seizure.

text.p: South Korea on Wednesday summoned Japan's ambassador to protest the seizure of a fishing boat by Japanese patrol vessels in disputed waters, a Seoul foreign ministry spokesman said.
Vice-Foreign Minister Lee Ki-choo called in envoy Shintaro Yamashita to lodge a formal protest over Tuesday's seizure and to demand steps to ensure the incident was not repeated, the spokesman said.
The trawler, Taeyang No. 102, was operating in waters recently claimed by Japan, ministry officials said. Japan last month held four South Korean fishing boats for similar reasons.

"A new fisheries agreement is being negotiated between the two countries and our position is that the existing agreement, which has been in force for over 30 years, must be observed," spokesman Lee Kyu-hyung told Reuters.
Japan in January expanded its territorial waters in accordance with a new maritime convention introduced by the United Nations in November 1994, he said.
The spokesman said Tokyo has told Seoul it would soon release the trawler and all 13 crew except the captain after an investigation.
Japan and South Korea have a troubled relationship stemming from Japan's 1910-45 colonial rule over the Korean peninsula. Frequent territorial disputes are fanned by ultra-nationalists on both sides.
Both countries claim sovereignty over barren outcrops of rock in the Sea of Japan midway between Japan and South Korea. The islands are called Tokdo in South Korea and Takeshima in Japan.
Japan has claimed the islands since 1905 when it signed an agreement with Korea that paved the way for colonisation. Seoul has stationed security police on the islands since 1954.
South Korea keeps a handful of permanent residents on the islands. Local historians say well-documented Korean claims to the islets date back to the year 512.
The main opposition National Congress for New Politics issued a statement on Wednesday demanding a Japanese apology over the seizure of the trawler.
